summary: Console usage analytics: sudden spike in 'unique_client_ids' metric with missing request_id causing inflated reported usage
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported a large unexplained increase in billed token usage visible in the Console's per-tenant usage breakdown for the last 24 hours. The Console's 'unique_client_ids' metric spiked ~6x overnight. Investigation found many ingestion records with null or empty request_id fields which the analytics join logic treated as distinct clients, inflating unique counts and rolling up to billing totals.

Impact:
- Invoice projection for Clipper Labs shows ~4.2x expected delta for the affected window.
- A subset of dedicated customers on the same ingestion shard may be seeing elevated unique_client counts on dashboards (visible to customers and internal billing UI).

Environment:
- Prod ingestion pipeline (us-east-1), dedicated tenants on vpool-7.

Observed behavior:
- Console shows spike in unique_client_ids and total_token_count for tenant clipper-labs between 2026-03-09 22:00 and 2026-03-10 03:00 UTC.
- Raw ingestion logs include many events with request_id = "" or missing header X-Req-Id.

Expected behavior:
- Events without a request_id should be deduplicated using client_id + timestamp window and not count as unique client_ids for billing aggregation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Query console usage API for tenant=clipper-labs between 2026-03-09T20:00:00Z and 2026-03-10T06:00:00Z using the v2/usage/breakdown endpoint.
2) Observe unique_client_ids time series and compare to token_count rollups; note disproportionate increase in unique count relative to request volume.
3) Pull ingestion logs from ingester-3 shard for the same window and filter where request_id is null or empty.
4) Run aggregation script used by analytics pipeline locally with and without a defensive join on request_id to reproduce inflated uniqueness when request_id is treated as primary key.
5) Confirm billing pipeline consumed the same aggregation outputs during billing-run at 2026-03-10 04:00 UTC (billing-run-id: BR-20260310-04).
logs: analytics-aggregator WARN 2026-03-10T01:05:21Z: join_key null for event id e3f2c9, treating as separate row
billing-run BR-20260310-04 log: consumed usage-aggregation partition p-15, total_token_count: 9,482,312, unique_client_ids: 1342 (expected ~312)
comments: Support (Jordan Hayes) — 2026-03-10: A customer (Clipper Labs) opened with a billing spike. Initial triage points to unique_client metric. Assigned to SRE for pipeline checks.

SRE (Mateo Ruiz) — 2026-03-10: Pulled ingestion tail on shard ingester-3; seeing many messages with missing X-Req-Id header from api-gateway v1.9.4. Suspect a regression in header propagation after the gateway restart 2026-03-09 21:50 UTC.

Analytics (Priya Nair) — 2026-03-10: Confirmed aggregator treats empty request_id as distinct. Temporarily changed the dedupe join to normalize empty/null to a sentinel ("__MISSING_REQID") for in-memory runs; preview shows unique_client_ids match expected counts.
Customer (Claire W.) — 2026-03-10: Appreciate the quick look — our finance team flagged the alert. Please advise if we should expect credits/adjustments.
Billing (Eve Park) — 2026-03-11: Placed a hold on auto-invoicing for clipper-labs pending adjustment. Need final confirmed corrected usage numbers before invoicing.

Engineering (Priya Nair) — 2026-03-12: Patch merged to normalize empty request_id during ingestion and update aggregation join logic. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/9876. Rolling to prod with canary 10% and verifying metrics.
Support (Jordan Hayes) — 2026-03-13: Confirmed with Clipper Labs that adjusted usage numbers reconcile with their own telemetry. Marking issue resolved. Billing to process adjustment.
Follow-up (SRE Lead - Arun B.) — 2026-03-13: Opened internal task to add better observable on header propagation failures and a defensive schema validation at gateway egress (INT-4122).
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: analytics aggregator sampling change introduced a regression. Rejected after sampling parameters unchanged.

Root cause: api-gateway v1.9.4 restart dropped X-Req-Id propagation for a subset of upstream proxy connections; ingesters recorded empty request_id and downstream aggregation join used request_id as primary dedupe key leading to overcounting.

Scope: Affected partitions processed by ingester-3 and ingester-7 between 2026-03-09T21:45Z and 2026-03-10T03:30Z. Approximately 8% of daily usage for tenants on vpool-7 may show inflated unique_client counts if not corrected.

Mitigation validated: Normalizing empty request_id before aggregation removes duplicates; re-running aggregation for the affected window produced corrected usage totals that align with customer telemetry.
Related signals: alert console.alerts/unique-client-spike fired for 5 tenants; cross-checked with billing-notify queue for potential invoice impact.
Related systems to monitor: api-gateway header-propagation metrics, ingester schema validation, analytics join logs, billing-run dry-runs.
Linked detection gap: no existing SLO on X-Req-Id propagation; adding monitoring and an SLO suggested as follow-up.
resolution: Deployed a three-part fix: (1) hotfix in ingestion to normalize null/empty request_id to a sentinel value (rolled at 2026-03-11 02:10 UTC), (2) aggregator join updated to prefer client_id+window when request_id missing, (3) api-gateway configuration corrected to restore X-Req-Id propagation. Re-ran analytics aggregation for the affected partitions and provided corrected usage numbers to Billing. Billing temporarily held invoices; credits/adjustments for Clipper Labs issued. Follow-ups: add header-propagation alerts and an SLO for request_id coverage (internal task INT-4122).
